data.long_meaning: The name Zacharias (Zachias) is derived from the Hebrew word ‘zachar’ meaning ‘to remember’. In the Bible, Zacharias is the name of a priest who is given a son in his old age by God in fulfillment of a prophecy. This name thus symbolizes the idea of being remembered by God and is a reminder of His faithfulness and covenant promises.

in_hebrew.name: זכיאס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: זכיאס הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוהים זוכר' או 'זכרון אלוקים'. השם מורכב מהמילים 'זכר' שפירושו זכרון ו'אלוקים' שפירושו אלוהים. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב יהודים ונוצרים כאחד, ויש לו משמעות רוחנית עמוקה בהקשר של האמונה באלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ζαχίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζαχίας είναι ένα όνομα που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός θυμάται' ή 'μνήμη του Θεού'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'Ζαχ' που σημαίνει 'θυμάται' και 'ίας' που αποτελεί τη μορφή του ονόματος του Θεού. Στο πλαίσιο της χριστιανικής παράδοσης, το όνομα Ζαχίας έχει ιδιαίτερη σημασία ως υπενθύμιση της δύναμης και της αγάπης του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Zachias
in_latin.long_meaning: Zachias nomen est quod significat 'Deus recordatur' vel 'memoria Dei'. Nomen ex hebraeo origine venit et in ecclesia christiana primitivam usum habuit. Zachias fuit etiam nomine cuiusdam principis publicani qui baptizatus est a Iohanne Baptista, secundum Evangelium Lucae.

in_english.name: Zachias
in_english.long_meaning: Zachias is a Christian name that originates from the Hebrew language, meaning 'God remembers' or 'recalled by God'. The name is derived from the Hebrew words 'zakar,' meaning 'to remember,' and 'El,' referring to God. In the New Testament, Zachias was a publican, or tax collector, who was converted by John the Baptist (Luke 19:1-10). The name holds significant spiritual meaning in Christian tradition, symbolizing God's remembrance and mercy. Throughout history, the name Zachias has been used across various Christian cultures, signifying a strong connection to faith and divine remembrance.

data.cultural_impact: Zacharias was a respected priestly name in biblical times and was mentioned in various books of the Old and New Testaments. It gained additional significance in the early Christian Church as Zacharias was among the priestly lineage of Jesus.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zacharias (Zachias) carries a deep spiritual significance as it reminds us of God's faithfulness to His promises. It acts as a reminder of the promises God has made to us, and serves as an encouragement to trust in His faithfulness, even in old age. It also symbolizes the idea of being remembered by God and cherished in His sight, just as Zacharias was when he was given a son in his Advanced age.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zachias, meaning "God remembers," is a name that symbolizes the promise of God's faithfulness in remembering His covenants and the faith of His people. It is a reminder of God's sovereignty and His unwavering commitment to remember and restore.

biblical_reference.note: Zachias was a chief tax collector in Jericho who was converted by Jesus.

historical_references.reference: The New Testament of the Bible mentions a man named Zachaeus, a chief tax collector in Jericho. He was a wealthy man and despised by the Jewish people. However, he was determined to see Jesus when He passed through Jericho. He climbed a sycamore tree to get a better view, and Jesus looked up and saw him and called him down. Zachaeus showed great faith and welcomed Jesus into his home. This event is recorded in Luke 19:1-10.

In the Old Testament book of Zechariah, there is a prophecy about a man named Zacchias (or Zerubbabel) who would be a faithful leader and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. This prophecy was given during the time of the Babylonian exile, around the late 6th century BC. However, the New Testament reference described above is more commonly associated with the name Zachaeus.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zacharias, which can be modernized to Zach or Zachary, has seen a resurgence in popularity across various platforms. Its biblical origins and association with strong, masculine figures have made it an appealing choice for parents seeking unique, meaningful names for their children. In social media, individuals with this name have built communities based on their shared heritage and nostalgia for the past. In the realm of baby names, Zacharias remains a top choice in many circles due to its historical significance and distinctiveness. Lastly, in literature, the name has been featured in numerous works as a symbol of strength and determination.
